startup.name: Agentcard
startup.description: Agentcard let's companies buy anything online. We work with companies building personal assistants to enable payments.

yc_acceptance.basis: Test note: this company was accepted to YC, so this is only the forward estimate. Starting prior is about 1 percent for a random applicant (0.6 to 2 percent third party range, per references/yc_acceptance.md). Agent payments is a current YC-style topic with real urgency (up), four person team (neutral), fintech and regulated cards are hard for a young team (down), and large incumbents Stripe, Visa and Coinbase are active (down). Net about 2 percent.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most likely say that card issuing for agents depends on banks and networks, that Stripe, Visa and Coinbase are shipping agent payment rails, and that the customer base of personal assistant companies is tiny and early. Without a regulatory path and live volume, partners may see a feature that incumbents will absorb.

bands.rationale: Small pre-seed of about 600K to 1.5M on a SAFE, barely above the YC deal. If few assistant companies sign on, a small round follows.
Typical 2026 seed near the 3.0M US median deal size and 18M pre money from PitchBook NVCA via Equidam (see stage_benchmarks.md). Early integrations with assistant builders attract a seed.
Strong seed led by a known fund, near the YC 2022+ announced median of 4.1M or above. A hot agent payments story draws a large round.
Upside seed or large first round if usage or revenue spikes, common for hot AI categories in 2026. Fast volume growth attracts a breakout round.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed step above 500K fails if card issuing and compliance take months, if the few personal assistant companies using it send little volume, or if investors see Stripe, Visa and Coinbase agent products as sufficient. Lyra and Bridgecard show virtual card startups raised little or stalled when issuing partners and chargebacks became hard.

bands.rationale: Small or bridge style A, or a down-ish A after a slow year. Volume is thin and revenue is interchange only.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A needs live volume and a defensible position. It fails if agent commerce stays small, margins depend on thin interchange, or issuer partners limit programs. Lyra shows no funding after its batch, while Slash reached A only by pivoting to a real customer base of online sellers.

bands.rationale: Modest C or growth round, or venture debt plus equity. Few fintech infrastructure companies reach this.
Typical C or later; 2022+ YC median C is 45M, D plus 97.5M. Needs licensing and scale.
Breakout later round at multi billion value. Needs category dominance.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C or later needs licensing, risk systems and large volume. It fails if the market consolidates into the networks and large processors, as with most card startups, and only top companies such as Slash and Jeeves reached these rounds after finding large customer segments.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Failure is most likely that agent payments stay a feature of Stripe, Visa and Coinbase, volume stays small and the company shuts down or is sold for talent. Lyra and Bridgecard show virtual card startups stalling. Upside needs a pivot into a broader spend or banking product, as Slash did.

killers.evidence: Stripe, Visa and Coinbase already announce agent payment products and have the distribution.
killers.mitigation: Serve assistant builders quickly with better APIs and controls.

killers.evidence: Card programs require bank partners, KYC and chargeback handling that stall small teams.
killers.mitigation: Use a licensed issuing platform and add controls first.

killers.evidence: Few personal assistant companies exist and their volume is small and uncertain.
killers.mitigation: Widen to any agent developer and consumer agent.

competition_now.name: Visa
competition_now.what: Network with intelligent commerce work for agents

technical_complexity.rationale: Virtual card issuing for agents requires bank partners, fraud controls and merchant compatibility. A four person team can build on an issuing API in three months, but handling declines, merchant restrictions and compliance is the hard part.

takeover_risk.rationale: These companies already announce agent payment products and have merchants, issuing and distribution, so absorbing this wedge needs only months and strong incentive.

evidence.claim: Agent builders need ways to pay online, and networks and payment firms are launching products for it.
Issuing APIs for virtual cards are a paid market today.

roadmap.proof: 1M monthly volume and low chargeback rate

roadmap.goal: Show recurring volume and revenue and add banks.

pros.evidence: Payment networks are building for it, confirming demand.

brand.name: Agentcard
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Agentcard" --era 2022+ : kind invented_or_proper, n=1826, alive 92.7 percent, exit 4.4 percent
brand.rationale: Agentcard is a descriptive compound that says exactly what it is, which helps early understanding but is weak as a brand and limits expansion. Past YC names like Slash grew beyond cards. Little effect on odds.

narrative.headline: Agent payments is timely but incumbents are close; seed likely, later rounds need a pivot or real volume.
narrative.general_summary: Agentcard offers cards so assistant products can buy things online. Timing is good and investors fund agent infrastructure, so a seed above the YC deal is more likely than not. The weakness is that Stripe, Visa and Coinbase are moving into the same space, card programs need bank and compliance work, and the customer base is early. Fintech analogs such as Lyra and Bridgecard stalled while Slash and Jeeves succeeded after finding large customer bases. The ladder follows the Fintech and B2B anchors with wide uncertainty.

assumptions: Blind forecast: only the YC listing text was used.
Seed means a round above 500K within about 12 months.
Fintech cohort is small; B2B anchors used as a cross check.
Recorded 2026 batch funding was not used as evidence.
